report: Reviewed the complete local_index_firewall claim and its sole implementation and test associations in sage_meta::todo. Requirements are: a stable crate-owned local-index identity; a private tracked map whose sole reader is keyed tracked lookup; permission for unrelated edits to rebuild that map and rerun cheap lookup; equal buckets backdated before header lowering, solving, normalization, and body checking; and impl-body edits leaving signature-level buckets unchanged. All these guarantees remain explicitly deferred by the implementation TODO. Captured local_syms/impls.rs confirms the stated prerequisite: local_impl_candidates is already tracked and trait-keyed, but recursively scans expanded module items, reads impl CST and trait_symbol, and lowers matching signatures within discovery. This is not the specified private-map/keyed-reader firewall, so existing tracking must not be credited as completion of this claim. The sole associated test, todo::solver_local_index_firewall, contains no assertions and is correctly classified TODO. Its comments specify the required persistent-edit observation matrix: separate index rebuild, lookup, lowering, solve, normalization, and body executions; unrelated-trait and impl-body edits stopping at equal lookup; relevant-trait/global-hazard invalidation; and stable identities. Those tests require the absent index architecture and observable persistent edit execution stages. Their deferral is justified by the matching explicit implementation TODO; no passing placeholder is behavioral evidence. No ordinary or N/A entries exist, no implementation or test code was changed, and no behavioral tests were executed. Commands executed were review start and review read (one out-of-bounds read failed before a successful whole-file capture), plus source-location discovery. This approves the accuracy and adequacy of the existing explicit deferral only, not an implemented incremental firewall.
